subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: Factory X produces 60% of all microchips for a brand, and Factory Y produces 40%. The defective rate of Factory X is 2% and that of Factory Y is 5%. A randomly chosen microchip from the inventory is tested and found to be defective. What is the probability that this defective chip was manufactured by Factory X?
explanation: By Bayes' Theorem: P(X) = 0.60, P(Y) = 0.40. P(Defective | X) = 0.02, P(Defective | Y) = 0.05. Total probability of defect P(D) = P(X)P(D|X) + P(Y)P(D|Y) = (0.60 × 0.02) + (0.40 × 0.05) = 0.012 + 0.020 = 0.032. Posterior probability P(X | D) = [P(X)P(D|X)] / P(D) = 0.012 / 0.032 = 12 / 32 = 3 / 8 = 37.5%.
